ApiError.description:
The body of every error the application answers, on every endpoint.

**`errorCode` is the contract; `message` is not.** Branch on `errorCode`; show `message` to a human. The wording of a message may change at any time. A message names the field and the rule that was broken and never echoes the offending value.

A `1005` that names a place in the request body also carries `field`, which is contract: where the refused value sits, in the notation the message begins with — dotted keys and `[i]` positions counted from 0, a header pair's name `[0]` and its value `[1]`, such as `rules[1].path` or `rules[2].response.headers[3][1]`. It names only keys the API defines and positions, never a key or a value sent. A `1005` about the body as a whole — a key the body may not hold — or about the `Authorization` header carries none, and so does every other error.

| errorCode | Name | HTTP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1000` | `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` | `404` |
| `1001` | `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` | `404` |
| `1002` | `SESSION_EXPIRED` | `410` |
| `1003` | `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` | `404` |
| `1004` | `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | `413` |
| `1005` | `INVALID_RESPONSE_CONFIG` | `400` |
| `1006` | `MALFORMED_REQUEST_BODY` | `400` |
| `1007` | `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | `415` |
| `1008` | `MISSING_REQUEST_CONTENT` | `400` |
| `1009` | `RECEIVE_URL_MOVED` | `410` |
| `1010` | `INVALID_SEARCH_WORDS` | `400` |
| `1011` | `SEARCH_TIMED_OUT` | `503` |
| `1012` | `SEARCH_BUSY` | `429` |
| `1013` | `INVALID_LIST_QUERY` | `400` |
| `1014` | `INVALID_SESSION_IDS` | `400` |
| `1015` | `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | `429` |
| `1016` | `LIST_BODIES_BUSY` | `429` |
| `1017` | `LARGE_BODIES_BUSY` | `429` |
| `1018` | `CAPTURES_BUSY` | `503` |
| `1019` | `TOO_MANY_CONCURRENT_CALLS` | `429` |
| `1020` | `TOO_MANY_REALTIME_CONNECTIONS` | `429` |
| `1500` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | `500` |

A published code is never renumbered, reused or given another meaning. New codes may be added; treat an unknown code by its HTTP status.

One exception to this shape: a request Node's HTTP parser refuses — broken framing, a chunked body it cannot read, request headers over 16 KiB or, on `qa-tools.ru`, over 100 lines (`431`) or never completed (`408`) — is answered `{ "error", "message", "statusCode" }` with no `errorCode`, and so is a path outside `/s/` that cannot be percent-decoded, such as `/api/sessions/%zz` (`400`). A client falls back to the HTTP status when `errorCode` is missing.

errorCode.description: Stable numeric code; see the table above.

message.description: Human-readable diagnostic. Not part of the contract.

field.description: Only on a `1005` that names a place in the request body: where the refused value sits, the start of `message` — dotted keys and `[i]` positions counted from 0, a header pair's name `[0]` and its value `[1]`. Never a key or a value the client sent.

SessionId.description: A session id, 43 characters: the access key to a public session, and one of the two a private session needs, beside its access key. Treat it as an opaque string. New ids are letters and digits drawn from a cryptographically secure source (about 256 bits); ids created before 0.20.3 may also contain `_` and `-`, and remain valid.

RequestId.description: The id of a captured request, a UUID v4 in lower case.

HeaderName.description: A header name: 1–128 bytes of the RFC 9110 token charset. Compared case-insensitively against the reserved list and `Location` (see `ResponseConfigInput`), and sent in lower case.

HeaderValue.description: A header value: at most 1024 bytes of visible ASCII plus space and tab (0x20–0x7E and 0x09). Empty is allowed. Sent exactly as configured. Because the charset is ASCII, `maxLength` here counts bytes.

status.description: One final HTTP status, 200–599 inclusive. Unregistered codes such as `299` are accepted.

headers.description: Ordered `[name, value]` pairs, at most 20, sent in this order. Duplicate names are allowed.

body.description: The exact text to return, as a string: JSON or anything else, announced by a configured `Content-Type`. `null`, `""` or absent means no body. At most 65536 bytes of UTF-8, no U+0000.

delayMs.description: Milliseconds to wait before answering, 0–30000. `null` is rejected.

template.description: Whether `body` is a template (1.9.0): with `true`, each placeholder in it — `{{request.id}}`, `{{request.method}}`, `{{request.path}}`, `{{request.query.<name>}}`, `{{request.header.<name>}}`, `{{request.body.<path>}}` — is replaced with that value of the request each answer is for, escaped for the answer’s `Content-Type`, the whole at most 65536 bytes. Every `{{` must start one of them, closed by `}}`, with nothing else inside the braces, or the response is refused `400` / `1005`. Absent or `false`: the body is sent exactly as configured, `{{` included. A JSON boolean only; `null` and `"true"` are refused.

ResponseConfig.description: A stored custom response. Every field is present at its effective value, never absent: a response created as `{"status":201}` reads back with `headers: []`, `body: null`, `delayMs: 0`, `template: false`.

body.description: The exact text returned, or `null` for no body.

template.description: Whether `body` is a template (1.9.0): its placeholders are replaced with values of the request each answer is for. `false` for every response saved without the key, those saved before 1.9.0 included.

CreateSessionRequest.description: The presence of `response` is the discriminant: present creates a custom session, absent a default one. `{"response": null}` is rejected with `400` / `1005`; omit the key instead. `queue` gives the session a response queue that starts at step 1; `{"queue": null}` is rejected too. `expiresInSeconds` gives it a lifetime; `{"expiresInSeconds": null}` is rejected too. `expiresAfterIdleSeconds` gives it an idle window; `{"expiresAfterIdleSeconds": null}` is rejected too, and so are `expiresInSeconds` and `expiresAfterIdleSeconds` together. `storeSourceIp: false` makes the session store no sender address; `{"storeSourceIp": null}` is rejected too. `rules` gives it response rules by path and method; `{"rules": null}` is rejected too. Any other top-level key is rejected with `400` / `1005`.

expiresInSeconds.description: The session ends this many seconds after its creation, whatever happens to it: no use moves its expiry, and `expiresAt` is that end. 60 to 604800 (7 days), so a lifetime only shortens a session. Omit it for a session that expires 7 days after its last use. A JSON number equal to an integer, such as `6e2`, is taken.

expiresAfterIdleSeconds.description: The session expires this many seconds after its last use instead of 7 days: every use moves its expiry this far ahead again, at most once an hour, or once a tenth of the window when it is under 10 hours. 3600 to 604800 (1 hour to 7 days). Omit it for a session that expires 7 days after its last use. Not together with `expiresInSeconds`. A JSON number equal to an integer, such as `36e2`, is taken.

storeSourceIp.description: `false`: the session stores no sender address, and every request it captures has `sourceIp` `null` — in the list, the detail, the events and the default answer. The headers the sender sent, `X-Forwarded-For`, `Forwarded` and `X-Real-Ip` included, are kept as sent. `true`, or the key left out, keeps the address. Set at creation only; `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}` gives it back. Only a JSON boolean is taken.

rules.description: Response rules the session starts with, as `PUT /api/sessions/{sessionId}/rules` takes them, checked after every key above and refused by its rules under `rules[0]` and on; `[]` is none. They share the 1 MiB body with `response` and `queue`: a full response and a full queue leave room for about 3 rules at every limit.

private.description: `true` makes the session private: it answers only calls that present its access key, `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. With no `Authorization` header the server draws the key and answers it once as `accessKey`; with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` the session is created under that key and the answer carries none; an `Authorization` that carries no key is `400` / `1005`, and nothing is created. `false`, or the key left out, creates a public session and ignores `Authorization`. Set at creation only. Only the JSON booleans are taken: `"true"`, `1`, `null`, an array or an object is `400` / `1005`.

ResponseChangeRequest.description: `mode` is required. `custom` answers with `response` from now on and saves it; `default` answers the default and keeps the saved custom response for a later switch back. A `response` beside `"mode": "default"` is rejected. Any other key is rejected. Every violation is `400` / `1005`.

QueueRequest.description: `steps` holds 1 to 10 responses, each checked by exactly the rules of `ResponseConfigInput`. A step that breaks one is refused with `400` / `1005`, its `message` and its `field` naming the step by its place in the array (`steps[1]`, the second; `queue.steps[1]` in a creation). Any other key is refused.

ResponseQueue.description: A response queue: 1 to 10 responses that answer the next captured requests one each, in order, before the session response answers again. A used-up queue stays here, with `next` `null`, until it is removed.

steps.description: The steps in order, each at its effective values.

next.description: The position, 1-based, of the step the next captured request gets, or `null` when every step has answered and the session response answers the next one.

total.description: How many steps the queue holds.

expiresAt.description: When the session expires unless it is used. Each use moves it a full idle window ahead, 7 days or the `expiresAfterIdleSeconds` it was created with, at most once an hour, or once a tenth of a window under 10 hours. For a session created with `expiresInSeconds`, the fixed end of its lifetime, which no use moves.

receiveUrl.description: The session's webhook URL: the webhook host and `/s/{id}`, `https://hook.qa-tools.ru/s/{id}` in production. Send webhooks here; `https://qa-tools.ru/s/{id}` answers `410` / `1009`.

private.description: Whether the session is private: `true` for one created with `"private": true`, which answers only calls that present its access key; `false` for every other, those created before 1.11.0 included. Set at creation only.

accessKey.description: The access key the server drew for a private session created without an `Authorization` header: 43 letters and digits, answered this once and never again. Keep it as a secret; QA Tools keeps only its SHA-256 fingerprint and cannot recover it. Absent for a public session and for one created under a key the call sent.

response.description: The response the session answers with: the custom one while it is active, `null` while the session answers the default.

customResponse.description: The custom response the session keeps, active or not, or `null` if it never had one. Equal to `response` while it is active.

queue.description: The response queue layered over `response`, or `null` when the session has none.

rules.description: The response rules, in the order they are matched; `[]` when the session has none, every session created before 1.3.0 included. A request the first matching rule answers takes no step of `queue`; one no rule matches is answered by `queue`, then `response`.

expiresAt.description: The expiry, already refreshed if this read moved it. For a session created with `expiresInSeconds`, the fixed end of its lifetime, which no use moves.

receiveUrl.description: The session's webhook URL: the webhook host and `/s/{id}`, `https://hook.qa-tools.ru/s/{id}` in production. Send webhooks here; `https://qa-tools.ru/s/{id}` answers `410` / `1009`.

expiresAfterIdleSeconds.description: The idle window the session slides by, in seconds: every use moves `expiresAt` this far ahead. 604800, 7 days, for every session created without `expiresAfterIdleSeconds`; `null` for a session created with `expiresInSeconds`, which does not slide.

lifetimeEndsAt.description: The fixed end of a session created with `expiresInSeconds`, equal to `expiresAt`, or `null` for a session that slides.

storeSourceIp.description: Whether the session's requests keep the sender's address: `false` for a session created with `storeSourceIp: false`, whose requests all have `sourceIp` `null`; `true` for every other, those created before 1.2.0 included. Set at creation only.

private.description: Whether the session is private: `true` for one created with `"private": true`, which answers only calls that present its access key; `false` for every other, those created before 1.11.0 included. Set at creation only.

response.description: The response the session answers with: the custom one while it is active, `null` while the session answers the default.

customResponse.description: The custom response the session keeps, active or not, or `null` if it never had one. Equal to `response` while it is active.

queue.description: The response queue layered over `response`, or `null` when the session has none.

rules.description: The response rules, in the order they are matched; `[]` when the session has none, every session created before 1.3.0 included. A request the first matching rule answers takes no step of `queue`; one no rule matches is answered by `queue`, then `response`.

SessionStatusRequest.description: The sessions whose status to read, and the access key of each private one among them. Any key other than `ids` and `accessKeys` is rejected. Every violation is `400` / `1014`.

ids.description: 1 to 50 session ids, each at most once. The answer keeps their order.

accessKeys.description: Optional. The access key of each private session among `ids`, by its id: `{"<id>": "<key>"}`. Every name must be one of `ids` and every value 43 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`, else `400` / `1014`. A private session whose key is not given here is `not_found`, as one that does not exist; a public session ignores a key given for it. The `Authorization` header plays no part in this read.

SessionStatus.description: The status of one session: `active` with what a list of sessions shows of it, `expired`, or `not_found` for an id that names no session — never created, deleted, or removed after it expired.

receiveUrl.description: The session's webhook URL, as `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}` gives it.

lastRequestAt.description: When the newest request the session holds was received, or `null` for none.

lastUsedAt.description: When the session was last used: its expiry minus its idle window, 7 days or the `expiresAfterIdleSeconds` it was created with. A use moves the expiry at most once an hour, or once a tenth of a window under 10 hours, so this may be up to that much behind the last use. For a session created with `expiresInSeconds`, whose expiry no use moves, the later of its creation and its newest request.

SessionStatusResult.description: One entry per id asked for, in the order of `ids`.

ResponseState.description:
How writing the answer to a captured request ended.
- `pending`: not finished, possibly inside its configured delay.
- `sent`: the backend finished writing the response into the connection. **Never a delivery confirmation.**
- `aborted`: the connection was gone before the backend finished writing — on a session with a configured delay, also when the sender ended its side of the connection before the answer.
- `failed`: the response was formed and writing it threw.
- `unknown`: derived at read time, never stored — still `pending` 60 seconds past its own `delayMs`: the server restarted inside a delay, or, on a session without a delay, the sender ended its side of the connection while its request was being stored.

New values may be added (see Stability); a client accepts a value it does not know.

QueueStep.description: The step of the session's response queue that answered a request: its position, 1-based, and how many steps the queue held then. `{"index":2,"total":7}` is step 2 of 7.

status.description: The status the backend composed; `null` only when writing failed before one was composed.

queueStep.description: The step of the response queue that answered the request, or `null` when the session response or a response rule answered it.

rule.description: The response rule that answered the request, or `null` when none did — the queue or the session response answered — and for every request recorded before 1.3.0. A rule and a queue step never answer the same request.

ResponseRecord.description: The answer the backend formed for a captured request and how writing it ended. Bytes use the same UTF-8/Base64 rule as the request body. `body: null` on all three body fields means no body at all, which differs from an empty body `""`. `raw` is the representation the backend formed, not a wire capture: `Date`, `Connection` and `Keep-Alive` are not part of it.

headers.description: The exact final ordered pairs the backend wrote, `content-length` included.

bodySuppressed.description: `true` when a representation was formed and not sent, which is `HEAD`.

queueStep.description: The step of the response queue that answered the request, or `null` when the session response answered it.

rule.description: The response rule that answered the request, with its method and path as they were when it answered, or `null` when none did, and for every request recorded before 1.3.0.

RequestListItem.description: One captured request in the list. Without `include`, lightweight metadata only: no body and no full headers. `include=headers` adds `headers`; `include=body` adds `body`, `bodyBase64` and `isBinary`, under the rule `RequestDetails` follows.

sourceIp.description: The address the sender connected from, or `null` when it did not parse or the session stores no sender address, as in `RequestDetails`.

path.description: The path the request was sent to, without the query string, exactly as sent, as in `RequestDetails`: `/s/{sessionId}` or a path under it such as `/s/{sessionId}/stripe/events`. `null` for old captures.

response.description: Summary of the recorded answer, or `null` when nothing was recorded.

headers.description: Only with `include=headers`: the headers as `RequestDetails` gives them, `[name, value]` pairs in the order received, duplicates kept.

body.description: Only with `include=body`: the body when it is valid UTF-8 (an empty body is `""`), `null` when it is not.

bodyBase64.description: Only with `include=body`: the body in Base64 when it is not valid UTF-8, else `null`.

isBinary.description: Only with `include=body`: whether the body is not valid UTF-8 and is in `bodyBase64`.

RequestDetails.description: The complete captured request. A body that is valid UTF-8 travels in `body` (`bodyBase64: null`, `isBinary: false`); any other body travels as Base64 in `bodyBase64` (`body: null`, `isBinary: true`). `raw` follows the same rule.

sourceIp.description: The address the sender connected from, or `null` when it did not parse or the session was created with `storeSourceIp: false`. A sender's own `X-Forwarded-For` or `X-Real-Ip` is stored as a header and does not change it.

headers.description: The headers exactly as the sender wrote them: each name in its case, in order, duplicates preserved, nothing added. A request captured before 0.36.0 passed through the HTTP proxy of `qa-tools.ru` and shows what that proxy forwarded instead: names in its canonical case, reordered, and sometimes an `Accept-Encoding: gzip` the sender did not write.

raw.description: The request line with HTTP version, the captured headers and the body.

path.description: The path the request was sent to, without the query string, exactly as sent: `/s/{sessionId}`, with its trailing slash if it had one, or a path under it such as `/s/{sessionId}/stripe/events`, dot segments, doubled slashes and percent-encoding intact. `null` for old captures.

httpVersion.description: The HTTP version the request arrived on: `1.1` on the webhook host, which speaks HTTP/1.1 alone, so an HTTP/2 sender falls back to it. A request captured before 0.36.0 shows the version of the proxy's hop, `1.1` whatever the sender used. `null` for old captures.

response.description: The recorded answer, or `null` when nothing was recorded.

RequestSearchRequest.description: What to look for in the raw requests of a session. Any key other than `words` is rejected. Every violation is `400` / `1010`.

words.description: 1 to 8 words. Each is looked for on its own, as the exact bytes of its UTF-8 encoding. A repeated word is answered twice.

items.description: 3 to 200 **bytes** in UTF-8, so at most 200 characters and fewer when they are not ASCII. Not split and not trimmed.

RequestSearchResult.description: For each word of the search, the requests whose raw request contains it. Ids only: read a request with `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/requests/{requestId}`.

matches.description: One list per word, in the order of `words`.

items.description: The ids of the requests that contain the word, newest first.

RequestHeaderCondition.description: Holds when one of the request’s headers has `name`, compared case-insensitively in ASCII, and exactly `value`, compared whole and case-sensitively. A repeated header matches when any of its occurrences does.

value.description: 0 to 200 **bytes** in UTF-8, without U+0000, as `headers` gives it: `123` does not match `1234`.

RequestQueryRequest.description: What to list. Every key is optional, and `null` is not an absent key; any other key is rejected. The conditions in `headers` and `body` combine with AND, at most 8 of them in all. `after`, `since`, `limit`, `order` and `include` mean what the query parameters of `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/requests` mean. Every violation is `400` / `1013`, except an `after` that names no request of the session, `404` / `1003`.

body.description: Body conditions: each holds when the stored body contains the string’s UTF-8 bytes exactly — case-sensitive, no wildcards, the bytes as received and not decoded from `Content-Encoding`.

items.description: 3 to 200 **bytes** in UTF-8, so at most 200 characters and fewer when they are not ASCII.

after.description: A request id: only the requests received after it, in the order they arrived, whatever `order` sorts them by. One that is not a request of the session — deleted, pushed out by the newest 1000, never one — or is not a UUID is `404` / `1003`. Not with `since`.

since.description: Only the requests received strictly later, compared with the time as stored, to the microsecond, though `receivedAt` shows milliseconds: a request's own `receivedAt` may list it again. To continue from a request already seen, use `after`, which never repeats one. A zone offset is required. Not with `after`.

limit.description: At most this many requests: 1 to 1000, or 1 to 20 with `body` in `include`, which makes 20 the default.

order.description: `desc`, newest first, or `asc`, oldest first; the id breaks ties in the same direction.

include.description: What to add to each request: `headers`, `body` or both.

WebhookDefaultAnswer.description: The answer of a default session: the stored request's id, then what was stored, each value as `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/requests/{requestId}` gives it, and the request's link in the inspector. Nothing of the request's body, headers or query string. Open to additive extension: ignore keys you do not know.

requestId.description: The stored request's id, equal to `X-Webhook-Inspector-Request-Id` and to its old name `X-QA-Tools-Request-Id`.

message.description: `Captured by QA Tools`; `Captured by Webhook Inspector` from the date the changelog's 1.19.0 entry gives.

inspectorUrl.description: The request on its session's page in the inspector, `https://qa-tools.ru/v/{sessionId}#{requestId}`: opened in a browser, it shows this request. It grants what the webhook URL grants, nothing more.

receivedAt.description: When the request was stored, as the list and the detail give it.

path.description: The path the request was sent to, as stored: `/s/{sessionId}` or a path under it, a trailing slash and percent-encoding as sent, without the query string.

bodySize.description: The body's size in bytes as received — a compressed body's compressed size — `0` for none.

sourceIp.description: The address the sender connected from, or `null` when it did not parse or the session stores no sender address, as in `RequestDetails`.

ResponseRuleInput.description: One response rule. A captured request whose method is `method` — any method when it is `null` — and whose path matches `path` is answered with `response`, and takes no step of the response queue. The first rule a request matches answers it; a request no rule matches is answered by the queue, then the session response. A rule that breaks a check is refused with `400` / `1005`, its `message` and its `field` naming it by its place in the array (`rules[1].path`, the second) and quoting nothing it holds; any other key is refused.

method.description: The method to match, as the receiver stores it, in upper case, or `null` for any method. One of the 34 methods the receiver accepts — `CONNECT` is not one. `HEAD` is a method of its own: a rule for `GET` does not match a `HEAD`.

path.description: The path pattern, matched against what follows `/s/{sessionId}` in the path as the request sent it: an exact path, or a prefix when it ends in `*` — `/items/*` matches `/items/1` and `/items/a/b`, not `/items`. Compared literally: case-sensitive, nothing decoded or normalised (`/%6Frders` is not `/orders`, `/orders/` is not `/orders`), the query string not part of it, and `/` for the session's own URL with or without its trailing slash; a request sent in absolute form, `POST http://hook.qa-tools.ru/s/{sessionId}/orders`, matches no rule. Nothing in it is special but a last `*`: `%`, `_`, `.` and every other character match only themselves. It starts with `/`, is at most 1024 characters of visible ASCII (`!` to `~`), holds no `?`, and holds `*` only as its last character: write any other character, a space or a letter outside ASCII, percent-encoded, as a request sends it.

RulesRequest.description: `rules` holds at most 20 response rules, in the order they are matched; `[]` removes every rule. More than 20 are refused with `400` / `1005` whatever they hold, then each rule in order by the checks of `ResponseRuleInput`, then any other key.

ResponseRule.description: One response rule as the session holds it, its response at its effective values.

method.description: The method it matches, or `null` for any method.

path.description: Its path pattern, as it was saved: an exact path, or a prefix ending in `*`.

RuleSummary.description: The response rule that answered a request: its position in the session's rules when it answered, 1-based. `{"index":2}` is the second rule.

RecordedRule.description: The response rule that answered a request, as it was when it answered: its position, 1-based, its method — `null` for any — and its path pattern. The response it answered with is the record itself.

SessionId.name: sessionId
SessionId.description: The session id. An id that is not 43 characters of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-` is answered exactly like an unknown session: `404` / `1001`.

RequestId.name: requestId
RequestId.description: The request id. An id that is not a UUID is answered `404` / `1003`.

RequestIdHeader.description: The id of the stored request, `X-Webhook-Inspector-Request-Id`. Absent on every error.

OldRequestIdHeader.description: The same id under the header's old name, `X-QA-Tools-Request-Id`, sent beside `X-Webhook-Inspector-Request-Id` until the date the changelog's 1.19.0 entry gives. Absent on every error.

NoSniff.description: Always `nosniff` on an answer to a `/s/…` URL.

SandboxPolicy.description: Always `sandbox; default-src 'none'` on an answer to a `/s/…` URL: a browser that opens it runs no script, submits no form and loads nothing for it, and the document gets an opaque origin. Webhook senders ignore it.

RateLimitLimit.description: How many calls of this kind one address may make in a minute: `60` on `POST /api/sessions`, `1200` on every other route under `/api`.

RateLimitRemaining.description: How many of them this address has left in the current minute, after this call: `0` on a refusal.

RateLimitReset.description: Whole seconds until the current minute ends and the count starts again, 1 to 60. The minute starts with the address's first call counted in it.

RetryAfter.description: Whole seconds to wait before calling again: until the minute ends after `1015`, and `1` after `1012`, `1016`, `1017`, `1018`, `1019` and `1020`. Absent on every other answer.

BadRequestBody.description: `1006 MALFORMED_REQUEST_BODY`: a body declared `application/json` that is empty or does not parse.

value.message: Request body must be a JSON object

NotFoundSession.description: `1001 SESSION_NOT_FOUND`: the session does not exist, the id cannot be one, or the session is private and the call did not present its access key. The three are indistinguishable.

value.message: Session not found

SessionExpired.description: `1002 SESSION_EXPIRED`: the session exists but has expired. It is not revived.

value.message: Session expired

PayloadTooLarge.description: `1004 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`: the request body exceeds 1 MiB (1048576 bytes), or 1 KiB (1024 bytes) on a route that takes no body.

value.message: Payload too large

UnsupportedMediaType.description: `1007 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`: the request declares a media type this endpoint does not accept.

value.message: Content-Type must be application/json
Internal server error

RateLimitExceeded.description:
`1015 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: this address has made its 1200 calls under `/api` for the minute, session creation not counted. Nothing was done; call again after `Retry-After` seconds.

`1019 TOO_MANY_CONCURRENT_CALLS`: this address already had 128 calls in flight on the API and the MCP server together, waits included. Refused at once, before the body was read, not queued; nothing was done. Call again after `Retry-After`, one second. Also in place of an answer that was ready but would have taken this address's answers not yet written past 16 MiB, or the server's past 64 MiB, while another answer of the address was still being written (an address's first is always sent): the call was carried out, and only its answer is this refusal. Call again after `Retry-After`, one second.

value.message: Rate limit exceeded: 1200 API calls per minute per address; try again in 42 s
Too many calls in flight: 128 at once per address; try again in a moment
Too many answers not yet written: 16 MiB at once per address; try again in a moment

accessKey.description: A private session's access key: 43 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`, which `POST /api/sessions` with `"private": true` draws and answers once as `accessKey`, or a key of that shape the creation was sent. Optional: a public session ignores it, and opens without it. A private session without it, or with another key, is answered exactly as a session that does not exist, `404` / `1001`. The scheme in any letter case; one or more spaces before the key; at most 256 characters in all.
